    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that eight teams have scored 26 or more points per game in the 2026 NFL season.
    • The Cowboys are the only team among those eight with more than two losses, and they have a 4-6 record.
    • "We have not been a good team and are a bad team," Jones stated Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that eight teams have scored 26 or more points per game in the 2026 NFL season. The Buffalo Bills (31.9), the San Francisco 49ers (31.2), the Cincinnati Bengals (30.9), the Jacksonville Jaguars (29.9), the Dallas Cowboys (28.6), the Detroit Lions (28.6), the Chicago Bears (26.8), and the Kansas City Chiefs (26.3).

    The Cowboys are the only team among those eight with more than two losses, and they have a 4-6 record. Dallas is one of only two teams with a scoring defense below league average, and theirs ranks 30th (28.2 points per game) out of the league's 32 teams. That's why Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones felt comfortably calling his squad "a bad team" on Friday.

    "We have not been a good team and are a bad team," Jones stated Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports. "At 4-6, that states everything you need to say. ... Does that mean we will play a bad game [and] be a bad team on Sunday? Not necessarily. And that's why we're trying to improve.".

    One way the Cowboys tried to improve their ailing defense this week was to strip first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and give them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. However, Parker will stay on with the team to run defensive meetings and build out the game looks, but the 34-year-old, the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, will not have the play-calling role defensive coordinators usually have on game day.

    "We've got a chance to play better doing it this way," Jones remarked of Dallas' demotion of Parker, via The Dallas Morning News.

    After Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in the 67-season history of the franchise, they now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).

    Third down conversion rate allowed.

    In a recent development, to be fair to Dallas' coaching staff, many of the defensive issues the last few years have been with the players on the field. Per CBS Sports Research, the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers.

    It has been revealed that jones' and head coach Brian Schottenheimer's handling of Parker is very weird, but the move could at least get Dallas to a 6-6 record after Thanksgiving. Dallas hosts the 1-8 Tennessee Titans in Week 11, then takes on the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

    Industry News: Timberwolves, Grizzlies reportedly hope to move to Eastern Conference after expansion; who makes more sense?

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two latest teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30.
    • Several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic.
    • Getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two latest teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30. Perhaps the biggest is geographic. Both Seattle and Las Vegas are located firmly in the western half of the United States. Should those cities eventually be granted teams, they would play in the Western Conference, leaving the league with unbalanced conferences. Therefore, someone in the West would have to move to the East in order to balance the conferences at 16 teams apiece.

    Several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic. While the Latest Orleans Pelicans are not out of the running, the likeliest teams to move in realignment, for now, are reportedly the Minnesota Timberwolves and Memphis Grizzlies.

    Getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels. Of course, there are obvious basketball reasons for preferring the East. Putting aside the decades of Western Conference superiority that hold little weight in the long run, the two teams best positioned to succeed over the next decade or so are the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. As the Latest York Knicks learned last June, the easiest path to a championship is avoiding Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander until they've already spent seven games battling each other.

    It has been revealed that but this isn't just a basketball conversation. The NBA, like most major American professional sports leagues, tilts east. There are simply more major cities in the Eastern half of the country than the Western half. Of the league's 30 existing teams, 17 play east of the Mississippi River: the 15 already in the Eastern Conference, along with the Timberwolves and Grizzlies.

    Recent findings suggest that travel is simply easier playing in the East. One projection of how many total miles each NBA team will travel this season has only the Miami Heat in the top half of the league, with the other 14 slots belonging to Western Conference teams. That projection has the Heat crossing 24 time zones, while every Western Conference team crosses at least 36.

    So Minnesota, Memphis and New Orleans are all incentivized to move, and with the Grizzlies and Timberwolves seemingly favored, let's evaluate the cases for each.

    The fundamental case for the Grizzlies is geographic. Memphis is further East than Minneapolis. As The Athletic points out, it is closer to more Eastern Conference teams as well, as it is within 600 miles of five East teams (Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks, Indiana Pacers, Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks). This not only makes travel easier for the Grizzlies, but for those teams as well.

    According to recent reports, while the Timberwolves are considered the better team right now, Memphis is probably the team better positioned to be competitive in the long run. Minnesota's best players -- Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu -- are all in their mid-20s earning market-rate salaries, and Rudy Gobert is much older at 34. Plus, the Timberwolves are essentially devoid of first-round draft capital.

    Recent findings suggest that the Grizzlies have a significant draft surplus, and their best players -- Cameron Boozer, Cedric Coward and Zach Edey -- are still on their rookie deals. If the idea is balancing the two conferences competitively, even if the Timberwolves have a higher immediate upside, the Grizzlies are probably the team we should expect to contend longer.

    According to recent reports, and then there's the matter of maintaining established rivalries. While neither the Grizzlies nor the Timberwolves are franchises steeped in historical success, Minnesota's last few years have established the Timberwolves as genuine postseason rivals to several crucial Western Conference teams. They've faced Nikola Jokiċ and the Denver Nuggets in multiple recent playoff series. They've faced Luka Dončić in multiple recent playoff series, even if they've come against different teams. Their series against the Spurs last spring included a Wembanyama ejection.

    The NBA may prefer to maximize the number of games Edwards plays against these high-profile opponents because there are existing narratives surrounding those matchups. In that case, keeping the Timberwolves in the West makes sense while allowing the Grizzlies to shift to the East.

    Sources indicate that minnesota's geographic case is a bit more nuanced. While Memphis is closer to more teams, Minnesota is closer to a few geographically convenient ones. If we assume for the moment that the new, 16-team conferences are going to come with four divisions featuring four teams each, Minnesota's proximity to Milwaukee, Chicago and Indiana makes for an easy four-team pod.

    In a recent development, the rest of the conference becomes remarkably easy to group from there. We have three more roughly Midwestern teams (Cleveland, Toronto and Detroit), five in the Northeast (New York, Brooklyn, Boston, Philadelphia and Washington) and four in the Southeast (Charlotte, Miami, Orlando and Atlanta). Just move one of those Northeastern teams to the Midwestern group -- presumably Washington, as it doesn't play in the existing Atlantic Division -- and you're set. If the NBA wants to make divisions a more prominent part of scheduling moving forward, Minnesota makes doing so much easier.

    There's also the idea of giving Edwards, one of the league's more personable stars, an easier path to the NBA Finals by getting him away from Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander. The NBA is, ultimately, a star business, and if stacking the deck in Edwards' favor helps build him up as one of the faces of the league, there is obvious appeal in doing so.

    By all accounts, we are far closer to resolution on a Las Vegas team than to the return of the Sonics in Seattle. Bidding has seemingly been more robust in Las Vegas, and an announcement is expected in the near future. If an announcement on Vegas comes before one in Seattle, there will be a brief period in which the NBA has an odd number of planned franchises.

    In a recent development, that does not mean that it will ever actually play a season with only 31 teams. Seattle, as commissioner Adam Silver has described, is much more of a turnkey operation than Las Vegas because of its arena situation and preexisting basketball history. In theory, a Seattle team could be announced much later than a Las Vegas team and still begin play in the same season. For now, the reported target for expansion teams to tip off is the 2028-29 season. However, if Seattle's bidding process takes too long for the two to begin play at the same time, or worse, if no Seattle group manages to put forth an acceptable bid in the near future, the possibility of one or even multiple seasons with 31 teams rather than the expected 32 probably does exist.

    Sources indicate that the NBA -- and every other major American professional sports league -- has had unbalanced conferences in the past. None do now. It creates scheduling headaches, and it's just blatantly unfair. Forcing some teams to overcome 15 opponents to reach the Finals while others only have to top 14 makes playing in the smaller conference too much of an advantage, and since the conference presently believed to be the superior one (the West) would be getting the Las Vegas team, competitive balance would go from a problem to an outright crisis.

    According to recent reports, fans have been calling for the abolition of conferences for decades now. Getting it to actually pass a vote would be harder. Realignment is voted on by the board of governors, so abolishing the conferences theoretically would be as well. Eastern Conference owners love having an easier path to the playoffs and the gate revenue those postseason games generate. This is where the idea of a season or two with just 31 teams in the league carries some appeal. It could give the NBA an opportunity to test the abolition of conferences provisionally with the idea that conferences would return when the league reaches 32 unless a new vote determines otherwise.

    The appeal of removing conferences altogether stems from the inherent fairness of a playoff system determined solely by record. There have been concerns about how removing the geographic component of playoff scheduling would affect travel, but there are potential solutions there. Returning to the "2-3-2" home-court format would minimize travel, or higher seeds could be allowed to select opponents in the early rounds to decide for themselves how they'd like to prioritize travel. The odds are obviously against the removal of conferences altogether, but expansion offers a potential opportunity to test it without committing to it long-term, and that's an opportunity the NBA would be foolish not to at least explore.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No.
    • In a recent development, lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline.
    • The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has declared the trade.

    In a recent development, lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

    The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

    Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

    Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

    Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

    According to recent reports, at worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

    According to recent reports, espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

    It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

    It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

    Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

    The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

    #50388. Essay: Escape – MX

    📅 06 Feb 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1955 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Spielverlagerung ↗ Open Full Page

    Essay: Escape – MX

    📅 06 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 06.02.2026 in den Kategorien Opinion mit 3 Kommentaren.
    • A few thoughts and reflections on the analysis bubble.
    • It has been revealed that humans want to understand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 06.02.2026 in den Kategorien Opinion mit 3 Kommentaren.

    A few thoughts and reflections on the analysis bubble.

    It has been revealed that humans want to understand. A fundamental need of our species eventually developed a concept for the desire to understand and to derive understanding: analysis. Carried through the centuries and applied primarily in literature, this drive increasingly found its way into the comparative physical activity of humans-sport. It fascinates hundreds of thousands of people every weekend; the urge to comprehend the logic – even where there is none – behind the results has become ever more omnipresent. Yet analysis existed long before people fully understood what analysis was – analyzing no longer becomes analysis simply because one is aware of doing it. Tracing the philosophical origins of analysis, pure analysis is merely a subform of communication: communicating by breaking down a whole into parts.

    Sources indicate that if we understand analysis as part of a larger communication context, it is hardly surprising that analytical formats in Europe developed primarily through blogs and digital platforms – parallel to the ongoing technologization of the world. Analysis has always existed, but only with the internet did it gain fresh relevance: communication could, for the first time, reach a potentially unlimited audience permanently. This explains an apparent contradiction of its origins: analysis exists continuously, yet it is always dependent on its recipients. Without an audience, it has no effect. In the words of Niklas Luhmann, communication does not arise from mere sending, but from understanding on the part of the receiver. Analysis is therefore not an isolated act, but an interactive process.

    In the age of social media, however, this dependence increasingly leads to a dead end. Highly complex matters are expected to be made understandable, consumable, and entertaining within thirty seconds. Paradoxically, social media produces more recipients than ever – and simultaneously a structural scarcity of attention. Georg Franck refers to this as the “attention economy,” in which visibility, rather than truth or depth, becomes the central currency. For a long time, analysis was a dialogical process: presenting, structuring, weighing – a reciprocal interplay between sender and receiver, reliant on resonance and reflection. Jürgen Habermas’ concept of communicative action captures exactly this: understanding emerges where arguments are given time and space. In short-form formats, communication continues- often with enormous reach- but the channels through which it occurs have shifted.

    Sources indicate that “A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.” – Herbert A. Simon.

    Analysis increasingly degenerates into a tool for tabloid-style exaggeration. Headlines such as “THE UPCOMING TACTIC,” “THE BEST PRESSING IN THE WORLD,” or “THIS IS MODERN FOOTBALL” suggest analysis but primarily follow market logic. Analyses are linguistically amplified as if they must be sold: the newest product, the best of its kind, faster, higher, further. Football as a consumer product is established – but now even the idyllic backyard of analysis? Marshall McLuhan’s famous dictum, “The medium is the message,” becomes particularly tangible here: the format determines not only the form, but increasingly also the content of analysis itself. The task is to reclaim analysis as a pursuit of understanding and curb its reduction to a consumable, attention-driven product – perhaps the challenge of the modern era is not to reinvent analysis, but to restore time, depth, and dialogical capacity to it.

    Sources indicate that to continue the metaphor of the idyllic backyard: analysis is increasingly turning into a bustling city. Here a street vendor, there a shop – no, I don’t want to buy anything. Help, where have I ended up? Everything crowded, everyone stressed, everyone caught in the rush of striving, of wanting. I just want the idyll: a coffee, some calm, a deep conversation. But the idyll is dead. Perhaps, as an analyst, one sometimes feels a certain emptiness – a metropolitan melancholy – the emptiness of overstimulated impersonality.

    “The metropolitan is compelled by the economy of money exchange to a precision and objectivity that deprives personal life of its warmth.” – Georg Simmel, The Metropolises and the Intellectual Life, 1903.

    But let us zoom out again: I often experience this feeling on “X” or YouTube. There is an abundance of information, often highlighted for attention. Yet more information on complex topics does not automatically lead to more knowledge; it generates noise – a noise I described earlier in the metaphor. This constant noise simultaneously depletes the already scarce resource of attention and creates a perpetual stimulus environment, leading to a lack of contextualization and interpretation, while leaving many exhausted-another tactic video, another tweet, another reel on the best pressing? Phew – this “phew” is what science calls fragmented cognition. Algorithms naturally amplify extremes-even in sports: outrage, “ALL-CAPS HEADLINES,” or promotion drive engagement.

    Sources indicate that this critique is not aimed at owners or analysts; we are all trapped in a system with incentive structures. Nevertheless, I want to draw attention to the growing bubbleization and ideological polarization of the analysis scene, amplified by extremes and a lack of contextualization. Quick accessibility and democratization lead to information, to knowledge, but this abundance also produces a depletion of theory and balance. We experience a pseudo – plurality in sport, an implied logic in the game that does not exist, manifested by algorithms – through likes and views.

    A concrete example: relationism. A fascinating topic, scarcely explored-yet the mere word triggers algorithmic attention so heavily that it is used excessively, reducing it to a black-and-white concept and establishing a dogma, rather than allowing proper theoretical discussion. How do we get out of this situation? Everyone has taste, everyone has preferences – yes, everyone has their dogmas. We are human – accept it. As René Marić once stated, dogmas can be dissolved by connecting them, by allowing different ideas to meet. Or as Jamie Hamilton puts it: perceive analysis as aesthetics. If we understand football as aesthetics, then football becomes art – but what is art? Art is the undefinable. And if we accept football as something without logic, we may at least free ourselves from established regimens of thinking and dogma. Don’t let yourselves be confined – feel the aesthetics.

    “We live in a world where there is more and more information, and less and less meaning.” – Jean Baudrillard, Simulacra and Simulation, 1981.

    It has been revealed that if we turn to history, literary philosophy shows us that even the concept of freedom divides opinion – does freedom enable analysis, or does it simply reinforce the status quo and thereby prevent true analysis? Perhaps, however, this is not the real question. Maybe it is not about freedom versus non-freedom, but about whether we understand logic as the opposite of freedom. Logicimplies binary outcomes – true or false, right or wrong – and this stands in tension with the ‘spirit of play’. Play has rules and objectives, yet within the act of playing there are no universal truths. The growing sense of uniformity and rehearsal – the impression that everyone plays in similar ways – often creates the feeling that the game follows the rules of a single, universal logic, as if logic determines play rather than play shaping logic.

    Recent findings suggest that my concern is less about what is objectively right or wrong in football, and more about how we, as analysts and coaches, sometimes present our ideas as universal truths. By doing so, we implicitly suggest that there exists a pure logic within the game – a logic that may not fundamentally exist. I would argue that sport exists primarily to evoke emotions in those who play and those who watch – an experience that can be understood through aesthetics, where art becomes a counterpoint to logic, as Tolstoy suggested. This challenges the belief that results or success should stand above everything else and dictate our styles of play.

    Sources indicate that if there is no single ‘true’ way to play, then there can also be no single true analysis that fully dissects it into definitive parts. That is why we must give space to the diffuse edges – even at the risk of weakening clarity or precision in our explanations – and accept that not everything can be clearly identified or categorized, because pure logic does not exist here. Yet I firmly believe that by allowing more room for uncertainty and ambiguity within the game, we open ourselves to entirely newly introduced worlds of understanding. And precisely for this reason, it is all the more important to ask ourselves who we are-and what we want to be as analysts. We must no longer divide ourselves into “us” and “them,” but understand ourselves as a shared form of football observer. Hannah Arendt describes thinking as an activity that only unfolds in exchange, as something that emerges in the “in-between” of people. Analysis, therefore, is not a possession, but a process. We need to dare more again: recognize our own (natural!) weaknesses in reasoning, disclose our personal assumptions, and discuss more honestly with one another. Know more of what we do not know and never will.

    According to recent reports, for this reason, I am skeptical of sharply distinguishing between universally trained and didactically trained analysts – or of job advertisements favoring only one type. Pierre Bourdieu shows that fields tend to stabilize through differentiation rather than understanding; separation becomes a social marker rather than a question of quality. Class war! Is that really what we want? Pitting the professionalization of sport against an open culture? This runs all the way from coach education to analyst circles: those who were never professionals are excluded. Those who do not meet the standards in general education also do not meet the standards in football. It is a coupling of market logic with football – and we need a return to open football, even if this openness, in some places, requires a degree of self-criticism that is uncomfortable for some decision maker. Breaking out of established logics also means accepting that logic cannot be predetermined.

    “Technology is never neutral; it always changes the conditions under which knowledge is recognized.” – Neil Postman, Technopoly, 1992.

    It has been revealed that attempts to standardize analysis this way lead to the imposition of linear thinking – a workflowization of analysis. The constant noise of information overload reinforces this effect. Increasingly, I observe a communicatively insulated bubble of club-based analysts, where external exchange is hardly desired. Yet the core of analysis is forgotten: “Thinking without communication is empty,” writes Jürgen Habermas-knowledge emerges in dialogue. Analysis thrives on joint dissection, on contradiction, and on critical (self-) questioning.

    This text is not a judgment of the scene. Rather, it is an expression of unease-a self-reflective judgment. I, too, have long allowed myself to be guided by factions, by the pursuit of jobs, by the pursuit of attention, and I became dependent on it. Only when I became aware of this and adopted a more didactic path – without a goal beyond curiosity about the game – did upcoming worlds of football open up to me. A curiosity expressed not in truths, but in provisional knowledge; in perspectives rather than dogmas; in theory as a tool rather than a label. Perhaps our strength should not lie in being faster, louder, or bigger. Perhaps it lies in withstanding the noise of the digital age. Where analysis no longer allows contradiction, it ends. But it also ends where analysis becomes mere consumption. But to end the text on a positive note – at the same time, there are more opportunities than ever before, more tactical cameras than ever, and more games to analyze than ever.

    It’s in our hands what we do with it.

    MLB rumors: Yankees moves heating up, plus latest on Tarik Skubal, Mets, Padres, Red Sox, more

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • It has been revealed that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • Industry observers note that the buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    It has been revealed that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below.

    Industry observers note that the buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set new records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records:.

    Industry observers note that 1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    Industry observers note that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    Industry observers note that 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    It has been revealed that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Industry observers note that given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.

    The Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.

    It has been revealed that acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs.

    In a recent development, the Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The upcoming extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    Melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.

    The Newly introduced York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.

    Industry observers note that loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.

    New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:.

    Industry observers note that "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting.".

    In a recent development, the 23-year-old Domínguez still has substantial-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.

    Lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the New York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.

    It has been revealed that the Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.

    It has been revealed that the Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.

    In a recent development, the New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.

    Hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

    #50384. Tech Report: Colts waive Daniel Jones: Indy not trading QB or Jonathan Taylor at deadline now a major second-guess

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (739 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Colts waive Daniel Jones: Indy not trading QB or Jonathan Taylor at deadline now a major second-guess

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mobb Deep said it best: "Ain't no such thing as halfway crooks.".
    • The Indianapolis Colts tried to sit on the fence at the 2026 trade deadline, ship away some (not all) expendable pieces, and land a somewhat respectable, middle-of-the-road record that might save a few jobs in the process.
    • Industry observers note that what's the old saying?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mobb Deep said it best: "Ain't no such thing as halfway crooks.".

    The Indianapolis Colts tried to sit on the fence at the 2026 trade deadline, ship away some (not all) expendable pieces, and land a somewhat respectable, middle-of-the-road record that might save a few jobs in the process. That meant moving on from the likes of DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, and Josh Downs, but holding on to Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones. Less than two weeks removed from that semi-fire sale, it's safe to say Indy botched it.

    Industry observers note that what's the old saying? If you're going to be a bear, be a grizzly. Well, if the Colts felt alright selling some pieces at the deadline, they should've stripped it down to the studs, knowing full well they are entering a rebuild anyway after firing GM Chris Ballard in mid-October.

    In a recent development, the losses have only continued to pile up for the Colts, which includes a demoralizing defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11. That game, which dropped them to 3-8, proved to be the straw that broke the camel's back for the Daniel Jones era, as the team has since waived the veteran quarterback.

    In a recent development, again, this is a player who teams were reportedly interested in leading up to the deadline. Instead of pursuing those opportunities to shed a sunk-cost under center, ESPN reports that Indy rebuffed trade interest from teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens.

    As a reminder, the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to acquire Kirk Cousins, while the Ravens shipped a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It's unclear what the compensation for Jones would've been, but I can tell you this—it's more than what they have now after waiving him: nothing.

    In the nine games before the deadline, Jones had the Colts at 2-7 while completing 60.3% of his passes, averaging just 191.3 passing yards per game, and posting a passer rating of 68.9. In total, Jones had tallied seven touchdowns and 13 turnovers.

    It was abundantly clear in the lead-up to the deadline that the two-year, $88 million extension the Colts signed Jones this offseason to was a disaster. Miraculously, a lifeboat drifted by them in the form of multiple teams inquiring about taking that burden off their hands, but they decided to stay on the deserted island. Now they're paying the price, with Jones set to account for $35.2 million in dead cap space for 2027 (provided he clears waivers) while the team pays him $49.8 million for 11 games played this season.

    Sources indicate that on top of Jones, Taylor, arguably the most sought-after prize on the trade market this cycle, should've been firmly on the block. With the Colts now without a clear answer at quarterback, Taylor is the living embodiment of that meme where the Lamborghini is sitting in the driveway of the trailer park.

    He was most valuable to Indy as a trade chip at the deadline, and that remains the case this offseason. The only difference is that any team acquiring him is getting a back that's a little older, has a little more mileage, and doesn't help them for this stretch run in 2026. That sets up a possibly diminished return this offseason if/when the Colts deal him compared to what they could've gotten at this deadline.

    For a team that won't have its first-round pick in 2027 after trading for Sauce Gardner at last year's deadline, they were in a position to refill the cupboard. Neither Jones nor Taylor likely would've fetched a first-rounder, but they would've given Indy premium ammunition for a later deal that could vault them back up. That level of asset mismanagement around the deadline now has the potential to ripple beyond just this second half of the season.

    Jones being waived is just one of the initial steps that the Colts will take as they embark on this rebuild and they tripped out of the gate. Whether it's firing Shane Steichen, trading Taylor, or eventually hiring a new GM (if they can find a taker), the organization needs to have a more definitive and realistic plan for its future so they're not looking back with major second guesses like they right now are following this deadline.

    • In a recent development, it took Indiana's star point guard a full season to recover from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, but sadly, his return lasted just four games before he headed back to the sideline.
    • For now, there is no firmer timeline than that, with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle saying in a recent radio interview that he didn't think it was "out of the question" that Haliburton would play in November, but he would not "put a hard date on anything.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Injuries have been one of the defining stories of the young 2026-27 NBA season, and while some teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder are unfortunately months away from relief, others are beginning to see a light at the end of the health tunnel. We're now nearly a month or so out from the early-season wave of losses, and on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania gave updates on the health of several key absent players. Let's use that as a launching point to check in on a handful of injured stars.

    In a recent development, it took Indiana's star point guard a full season to recover from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, but sadly, his return lasted just four games before he headed back to the sideline. Haliburton was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain in October, and according to ESPN, he will be sidelined for at least the next couple of weeks.

    For now, there is no firmer timeline than that, with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle saying in a recent radio interview that he didn't think it was "out of the question" that Haliburton would play in November, but he would not "put a hard date on anything.".

    Haliburton looked mostly like himself in the four games he played early this season, averaging just under 22 points and 10 assists. The Pacers have fallen to 5-10 and the Eastern Conference's No. 10 seed without him, and they are seemingly aware of the need for reinforcements. The Pacers "clearly are looking at doing something" on the trade market, with an upgrade on the wing viewed as a strong possibility, Jake Fischer stated Friday on SiriusXM NBA Radio.

    According to recent reports, A return to action seems further off for Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who had knee surgery in late October. Edwards spoke with reporters Thursday and mentioned he has "no clue" when he'll be able to return to the floor and declined to offer a timetable, per ESPN.

    According to recent reports, edwards missed 21 games last year and dealt with a knee concern in the postseason. Despite a hot start, that included a 47-point outburst against the Cavaliers, Edwards continued to experience discomfort in the knee, prompting the team to choose the surgery route rather than have their superstar continue playing through pain.

    Industry observers note that "It needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows? Maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good.".

    Industry observers note that led by LaMelo Ball, the Wolves have excelled even in Edwards' absence. At 11-5, Minnesota sits at No. 5 in the Western Conference standings entering their game against the Grizzlies on Saturday.

    Industry observers note that leonard has played just twice this season due to knee swelling, but according to Charania, there is optimism that he will return within the next few weeks. Leonard has been dealing with patellar tendinopathy, more commonly known as "jumper's knee," TSN reported on Tuesday. That is the same issue he dealt with throughout his 2019 championship season. SportsNet confirmed that reporting, while noting that swelling is not typically how that injury presents. SportsNet's reporting indicates that the swelling and jumper's knee are separate complications.

    Industry observers note that the good news on this front is that the reporting to this point indicates that the Raptors do not expect these concerns to linger once Leonard returns. Toronto successfully managed Leonard's health through that title season, and is being cautious to start this year as well. However, his absence has certainly been felt as Toronto is in the midst of a six-game losing streak without him.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, the player Leonard was traded for is just about ready to make his Clippers debut. Brandon Ingram is expected to return Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to Charania. Ingram suffered a partially torn Achilles tendon last season, which kept him out of the Clippers' lineup at the start of this year. His absence has been keenly felt in Los Angeles as the Clippers have scuttled to a 4-10 start without him. Los Angeles has both a bottom-eight offense and defense so far this season, so getting Ingram on the court should represent a helpful talent infusion.

    In a recent development, san Antonio's second-year star thankfully avoided a major injury when he fell on the court against the Clippers on Thursday. He will, however, miss 1-3 weeks with a left hip rotator strain. Harper was walking without a limp following the injury, per The San Antonio Express-News, a positive sign for his recovery.

    The Spurs have the NBA's best record at 13-3, but the story to watch as Harper rests is the performance of former All-Star De'Aaron Fox. Just beginning a four-year max contract, Fox has scored just 23 points in his last three games combined. He's averaging the fewest points and assists of his career since his rookie season. The Spurs had been starting their three high-profile guards -- Fox, Harper and Stephon Castle -- together early in the season. It was working, but with the caveat that that group never played a second without Victor Wembanyama. The Spurs are more than 40 points per 100 possessions better when their MVP candidate is on the floor.

    If Fox can't right the ship while Harper is out, that could open the door to San Antonio moving him to the bench upon Harper's return. The Spurs thrived last season with two ball-handlers, two shooters and Wembanyama in their starting lineup. The three guards are working because basically anything works with Wembanyama, but when the competition gets stiffer in the playoffs, it's going to be harder to get away with so little shooting in the starting lineup. That puts the onus on Fox to prove he still belongs in the starting lineup, and bouncing back while Harper is out will be a big part of that.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball.
    • In a recent development, most such decisions are easy and obvious.
    • All that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That important date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    In a recent development, most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    All that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    The 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder glitch this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a upcoming team before Opening Day.

    As a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout challenges. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    On the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    The Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 big-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    According to recent reports, A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028. Raley's power against righties and an extra year of control could make him a solid bench option moving forward.

    The regular season rolls on in the NFL with Week 11 already underway after the Houston Texans' victory over the Indianapolis Colts kicked things off on Thursday. Now, we have the rest of the slate on deck. While this is the smallest collection of games that we'll have this season (13) thanks to six teams being on a bye, it packs quite a punch. That includes a potential NFC Championship preview between the Vikings and 49ers in Mexico City.

    Industry observers note that of course, as is the case with every week in the NFL, injuries are a substantial piece of the puzzle and remain a big storyline heading into each contest. This week, there are some heavy-hitters that headline the injury front. Namely, the Chiefs will once again be without star running back Kenneth Walker III, while Niners standout receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) still has his status up in the air.

    It has been revealed that as teams across the league wrap up their week of practice, they've unveiled their final injury reports along with game statuses. Below, you can find updates for every game in Week 11.

    Note: Atlanta, Cleveland, Green Bay, Los Angeles (Rams), Latest England, and Seattle are on the bye in Week 11.

    All lines via DraftKings; All times ET.

    Breaking: De schaduwzijde van relationisme (in de Nederlandse bekerfinale)

    📅 06 May 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 06.05.2026 in den Kategorien Eredivisie,SV Academy,Tactical Theory,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • Nijmegen kon dit seizoen vanwege hun relationistische patronen en hun oplossingsstrategieën tegen mandekkingen met verticale positiewisselingen van hun centrale verdedigers op zich attent maken.
    • speelde vanuit een 1-3-2-4-1 in balbezit en drukvol met man-tegen-man pressing, waarbij Linssen de keeper van AZ boogvormig aanliep.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 06.05.2026 in den Kategorien Eredivisie,SV Academy,Tactical Theory,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

    It has been revealed that N.E.C. Nijmegen kon dit seizoen vanwege hun relationistische patronen en hun oplossingsstrategieën tegen mandekkingen met verticale positiewisselingen van hun centrale verdedigers op zich attent maken. Op de voorlaatste zondag ontmoetten zich in Rotterdam voor de Nederlandse bekerfinale AZ Alkmaar en het verrassende team van Nederland, N.E.C. Nijmegen. AZ won na een doelpunt uit een standaardsituatie in de eerste helft en goed uitgespeelde counters in de tweede helft uiteindelijk duidelijk met 5:1. Als kenner van de Nederlandse voetbalwereld heeft HH zich met de wedstrijd beziggehouden en beide teams nader onder de loep genomen.

    N.E.C. speelde vanuit een 1-3-2-4-1 in balbezit en drukvol met man-tegen-man pressing, waarbij Linssen de keeper van AZ boogvormig aanliep. Over het algemeen probeerde N.E.C. bij elke gelegenheid door te drukken en in hun 1-1-structuur te komen. AZ had zich daarop ingesteld en hun 1-4-2-3-1-achtige basisformatie veranderd in een soort 1-4-2-2-2, waarbij Parrot en Daal de voorste linie vormden. AZ’s idee voor lange ballen tegen Nijmegens klassieke 1-1-pressing (intentie van balverovering in het directe duel door maximaal korte afstanden, onafhankelijk van dekking van de centrale, binnenste lijn) waren dwars- en diepteloopbewegingen tegen Nijmegens driemansdefensie (afgestemd op AZ’s 1-4-2-3-1), om maximaal veel verdedigers van Nijmegen te binden en vrije ruimtes naast en voor de laatste linie maximaal groot te maken. Daarbij driften Mijnans en Smit steeds weer slim in mogelijke kaats- of doorverbindingsruimtes voor en naast Parrot. Omdat Nijmegen vrijloopbewegingen direct volgde en geen collectieve laatste linie en hoogte koos, werden de verticale afstanden sterk uitgerekt. Vooral Sandler als centrale verdediger en directe tegenstander van Parrot fungeerde soms als libero ver achter zijn medeverdedigers. Een groot manco bij N.E.C. was sowieso dat een collectief opschuiven van de laatste linie, de organisatie van een gezamenlijke nieuwe hoogte niet of slechts zeer terughoudend en twijfelend plaatsvond. AZ maakte daar gebruik van met slimme loopwegen achter de lijnen en/of snel uitspelen van combinaties in de (grote) ruimte voor de laatste lijn van N.E.C.

    De uitrekking en tegelijkertijd de fysieke aanwezigheid door Mijnans en Smit evenals de strijdlustige dubbele zes van Koopmeiners en Clasie kwam het 1-4-2-2-2 van AZ meer tegemoet. Soms leek het alsof juist deze verticale uitrekking (1-4-2-2-2, loopwegen van Parrot diep/wegtrekkend, Nijmegen zonder eigen buitenspellijn) evenals horizontale uitrekking (dwarslopen van Parrot, asynchroon/ aansluitend uitwijken van Mijnans) bewust door AZ gewild en voorbereid werd, doordat men vanuit een zeer brede 1-4-2-opbouw direct en vroeg lange passafstanden naar doelman Owusu-Oduro koos om het onmiddellijke aanlopen van Nijmegen (Linssen, waarbij de afstanden te groot waren om de bal serieus te kunnen onderscheppen) uit te lokken en daardoor eigen lange ballen goed te kunnen voorbereiden.

    In a recent development, wanneer AZ zich toch voor een korte opbouw besliste, vielen ze terug in een soort 1-3-1-opbouw met een naar binnen kwamende linkerback (de Wit). Opvallend was echter de duidelijke focus op de voorbereiding van lange ballen. Zo zocht bijvoorbeeld Koopmeiners in 1-3-2-opbouwmomenten, in plaats van de vrije ruimte te bezetten om druk te ontlasten, de directe weg naar voren om aanwezigheid voor tweede ballen te tonen.

    AZ’s hybride 1-4-2-3-1 naar 1-5-2-2-1 als kryptoniet tegen N.E.C.

    According to recent reports, bij balbezit van Nijmegen koos AZ voor een fundamentele spiegeling van N.E.C. Daarbij kozen zij voor een conservatief, mandekkend middenveldpressing. Terwijl Clasie (een zes van N.E.C.) en de beide tienen Daal en Mijnans (respectievelijk de halfverdedigers Dasa en Fonville) zeer klassiek vanuit het middenveldpressing balnabij mandekten en man-georiënteerd aanliepen, koos Parrot steeds weer slim voor diepere, passieve posities om alle wegen naar het centrum te sluiten.

    Een bijzondere rol kwam toe aan Koopmeiners. Hij ging, uitgaande van een manoriëntatie tegen Nijmegens creatieve speler Chery, steeds weer bij de overgang naar een lager blok in de laatste linie en vormde zo een vijfmanslijn. In totaal ontstond zo een 1-5-2-2-1 in lagere fases van AZ door het terugvallen van Smit naar de dubbele zes met Clasie. Chery werd zo niet per se extreem mandekkend bewaakt, maar zijn actieradius naar voren werd beperkt en tegelijkertijd werd het noodzakelijke uitstappen van Koopmeiners uit de vijfmanslijn goed opgevangen.

    Industry observers note that de 1-5-2-2-1-structuur van AZ paste ook bij de meer relationistische intentie van N.E.C., waarbij het minder ging om balgeoriënteerde vrijloopbewegingen ten opzichte van elkaar, maar meer om vrij-radicaal een overtal in balnabijheid te creëren, minder afgestemd op elkaar of in relatie tot specifieke tegenstanderbewegingen/-posities. Zo kon de niet-balkant tien van AZ het centrum mede sluiten, loopwegen uit de opbouwlijn van N.E.C. onderscheppen en N.E.C.’s zessen dwingen om breder buiten het blok te spelen of hoger te positioneren, waardoor ze minder bij overtal situaties betrokken waren of de restverdediging verwaarloosden.

    Tegelijkertijd was hij in de counter snel aanspeelbaar (korte maar verleggende passafstanden tegen counter-press na balwinst). De beide tienen van AZ waren verantwoordelijk voor het oppakken van de steeds weer verticaal opschuivende centrale verdedigers van N.E.C. In totaal slaagde AZ erin met deze structuur een +1 in de laatste linie te creëren, doordat Clasie zich dieper en eerder aan de niet-balkant tien (Lebreton) oriënteerde, Goes in de laatste lijn +1 tegen Linssen kon doorschuiven, de ruimte voor de verdediging met Smit werd verdicht en de beide centrale tienen het centrum sloten. Daarbij werd er minder geprobeerd om directe balveroveringen te realiseren, maar des te meer om acties naar voren te blokkeren en de balbezitter passief te controleren. Het leek alsof AZ langer probeerde de controle over posities en ruimtebezetting ten opzichte van elkaar te behouden dan N.E.C. dat met hun vele positiewisselingen en herstructureringen kon.

    Industry observers note that wanneer AZ toch het pressingmoment activeerde, paste dat goed bij de opbouwstructuur van N.E.C. Meestal koos Parrot dan een centrum-sluitende, iets laargere positie ten opzichte van Sandler of een centrale verdediger van N.E.C. Wanneer N.E.C. vervolgens via de halfverdedigers indribbeld, werden de afstanden in hun eerste opbouwlinie automatisch groter. Het indribbelen van de halfverdedigers kon door de tienen van AZ goed worden opgevangen, een terugpass werd in de beweging door de eerder uitgestapte tien doorgelopen en Parrot nam verticale vervolgbewegingen van de passerende halfverdediger over. Door de grotere passafstand (door het vroege indribbelen) werd de loopactie van de passer minder effectief, omdat de bal langer onderweg was en de druk van AZ op (meestal) Sandler goed kon worden behouden. Korte passafstanden bij N.E.C. voor een lokkend spel en bewegen werden zo opgelost, mede omdat Nejasmic in pressingoplossingen als derde man geen sterke prestatie leverde. AZ liep echter vaak niet door tot Cillessen, die desondanks vaak zonder druk voor de lange bal koos (die zoals eerder beschreven geen effectief middel was).

    Sources indicate that zonder indribbelen liep het voor N.E.C. ook niet beter, want doordat Sandler graag vanuit diepere posities lange passes probeert te spelen (Schlotterbeck-Vibes), moet N.E.C. bij het opschuiven grotere afstanden overbruggen met de laatste linie. Dit lukte slechts onregelmatig, waardoor de aansluiting van de laatste linie onvoldoende was.

    Recent findings suggest that desalniettemin liet N.E.C. in de eerste helft, vaker via rechts, goede aanzetten zien om vanuit de zijkanten kansen te creëren. Een aanvallend probleem dat zich gedurende de hele wedstrijd voordeed, was dat acties vanaf de zijkant naar binnen niet ruimer (dus dynamisch ruimtes richting het centrum openen) of doelgerichter (loopacties in de rug van de balkant centrale verdediger) werden bevoordeeld. De aansluitende bewegingen om tegenstanders bewust weg te trekken van de vrijgespeelde zijkant kwamen te weinig voor. In plaats daarvan werden mogelijke passroutes naar binnen soms dichtgelopen door passief achter de bal aan te lopen (om een korte passoptie te zijn?). Een “Escadinha”, dus een diagonale positionering van meerdere spelers als een “ladder” naar voren, idealiter richting het doel, zou ook een goed middel zijn geweest om de relationistische patronen van N.E.C. om te zetten in gevaarlijkere situaties voor het doel, maar werd niet gecreëerd. Vooral via Sano als vrije, hoger doorschuivende, licht niet-balkant zes had men via een precieze halfspace-halfspace-verplaatsing (tegen mandekkingsteams sowieso altijd effectief) tot afwerkposities kunnen komen. Vooral links met Koopmeiners en rechts met Goes, die beiden bezig waren met het dekken op de lijn van de balkant nummer tien van N.E.C., had men goed ruimtes in hun rug kunnen bezetten en bespelen – zowel achter als voor de laatste linie van AZ. Een paar keer, wanneer het N.E.C. lukte om van buiten naar binnen achter de balkant centrale verdediger te opereren, werd het ook meteen gevaarlijk. Op die momenten werden door de duo’s van N.E.C. (N.E.C. gebruikt de duo’s op de zijkant enigszins vergelijkbaar met Bayern in voor- of achterlopende, doorlopende bewegingen) (Ouaissa-Chery/Dasa en Önal-Lebreton/Fonville) natuurlijke verdedigingsmechanismen uitgelokt (achter de back spelen = centrale verdediger die uitstapte zal waarschijnlijk in de laatste lijn terugvallen, afdekken of doordekken), waardoor N.E.C., gecombineerd met goed wegbewegen van de tegenstander, zich in de rug van de verdediging enkele (halve) kansen kon creëren. AZ loste deze kleine problemen in de controle op doordat Clasie zich als niet-balkant zes toch meer balgeoriënteerd positioneerde, en Lebreton minder klassiek volgde.

    Recent findings suggest that lange ballen van N.E.C. tegen een al terugzakkend AZ, dat snel naar achteren liep om diepte te sluiten, waren niet kansrijk – noch dynamisch noch numeriek.

    Industry observers note that in de tweede helft probeerde N.E.C. meer via een opdribbel van Fonville over de linkerkant te overloaden. Nejasmic koos een duidelijk meer centrumhoudende positionering in balbezit (zessen gestaffeld), Lebreton speelde als linker wing-back, de ingevallen Willumsson iets dieper, vermoedelijk om Goes van AZ uit de verdediging te trekken. Sano, de oprukkende Fonville en gedeeltelijk ook Chery namen deel aan de overload links. Een intentie leek te zijn om links aan te lokken om vervolgens rechts uit te spelen en Ouaissa in 1-tegen-1-duels te krijgen. Koopmeiners volgde Chery echter niet consequent, N.E.C. stond gedeeltelijk met 6-7 spelers in de linker halfspace, omdat zelfs Dasa (!) naar die kant ging. De bewegingen in deze overload waren echter zelden goed genoeg op elkaar afgestemd. De nog steeds aanwezige ruimtes (ook omdat AZ al vroeg balnabij met hun 4/5-mansketen kantelde en beide backs de Wit en Dijkstra individuele zwaktes hebben in het verdedigen van de rug) van buiten naar binnen in de rug (achter of voor de verdedigingslinie van AZ) van de half-uitstappende Goes werden te zelden consequent bespeeld of pas te laat bezet. Voorwaartse, boogvormige bewegingssequenties rondom een doelspeler, die positiegetrouw een ruimte bezet en als kaatsspeler fungeert, werden niet ingezet, waardoor alle bewegingen ten opzichte van elkaar geïmproviseerd of fragmentarisch leken. Wanneer men er eenmaal in slaagde een pocket in de halfspace tussen meerdere AZ-spelers te openen, werd deze geopende ruimte niet verder benut door bijvoorbeeld een tegenstanderbindende loopactie achter deze ruimte, maar probeerde elke speler eerder een beetje dominant de bal op te halen en verder te passen. Kort gezegd waren er veel dominante spelers die allemaal graag de bal direct en zonder intentie van elkaar wilden hebben. Aanvullende, ondersteunende intenties bij spelers waren zeldzaam. Waar men in de eerste helft nog vroeg een flankbezetting koos en zo een duo op de flank ruimte gaf, was Linssen nu de enige speler van N.E.C. in de box tegen AZ, dat consequent een +1 behield. Wanneer N.E.C. via de goed, maar nog te terughoudend, niet tot het einde van het mogelijke oprukpotentieel indribbelende Fonville wist op te rukken, ontbrak het aan activiteit en aansluitende bewegingen om via een snelle korte verplaatsing van afzakkende/verbindende zessen/centrale verdedigers de ontstane ruimtes in het centrum te bespelen. Vooral Willumsson bood hier geen goede passopties, hoewel hij zich in kansrijke ruimtes bevond. Ondanks het gebrek aan doorbraak kon N.E.C. meer controle over de wedstrijd verkrijgen en AZ enigszins naar achteren drukken. AZ daarentegen ging vanaf ongeveer de 55e minuut als reactie agressiever pressen, Goes volgde in hogere middenveldpressingfasen Willumsson ver naar voren. N.E.C. slaagde er niet in om tijdig in mandekking-oplossende patronen te komen, ook het spel via de extra speler Cillessen bracht geen verlichting. De communicatie van Sano en Nejasmic met betrekking tot afgestemd vrijlopen en vrijmaken, bewegingen naar de bal, liet te wensen over.

    According to recent reports, de invalbeurt van Willumsson bracht echter defensieve meerwaarde. De 193 cm grote IJslander kon bij lange ballen van AZ meer ruimte afdekken en met grotere actieradius meer aanwezigheid tonen bij tweede ballen, zonder gaten in de mandekking als tien op AZ’s zessen te trekken. N.E.C. paste namelijk Nejasmic aan in de rol van ondersteunende speler van Sandler. De zes koos nu zijn positioneringen zodanig dat hij direct rond/met Sandler tegen Parrot verdedigde en hem afschermde, waardoor vaak een soort viermanslijn bij N.E.C. ontstond, wat AZ voorlopig in toom hield.

    In a recent development, N.E.C. probeerde nog steeds van links naar rechts uit te spelen. Helaas moesten ze de problemen in de restverdediging evenals de lasten van hun over-overload duur bekopen, omdat AZ twee keer na een verplaatsing naar Ouaissa balveroveringen boekte, counters startte en N.E.C.’s individuele rest-mandekking uiteindelijk meedogenloos afstrafte met de doelpunten voor 2:0 en 3:0. Vooral bij het tweede doelpunt werd duidelijk dat de individuele oriëntatie op de tegenstander, bijna onafhankelijk van de balpositie op het veld en zonder collectieve afstemming, duidelijke nadelen met zich meebrengt. Sowieso is mandekking rond het eigen zestien een minder logisch middel – zonder baldruk en collectieve hoogtebepaling van een laatste verdedigingslinie wordt het een uitnodiging om kansen te creëren. Bij de 2:0 door Mijnans lag het centrum voor het doel van Nijmegen open, bij de 3:0 werd er niet onderling gekanteld. Aan beide doelpunten ging echter een overloadpoging links vooraf, beter gezegd een over-overloadpoging. Klassieke overloadings met één, misschien twee extra spelers hebben als effect de tegenstander (idealiter) kort in een buitenruimte te binden zonder dat hij toegang tot balverovering heeft, vervolgens in voorbereide structuren (passafstanden zo groot als mogelijk voor zo min mogelijk balstops, maar zo kort als nodig om het overloadingseffect te benutten) te verplaatsen en de vrijere kant via 1-tegen-1, kleine-aantallenpatronen of voorzetten uit de halfspace te benutten. Bij een over-overload in de zin van het relationisme gaat het minder om goed gebalanceerde verplaatsingsstructuren, kleine-aantallenpatronen op de vrijere kant of een gezonde numerieke verhouding, maar om het doorspelen aan de overload kant. N.E.C. over-overload links, verplaatste dan relatief ruim (dus niet kort) via de centrale verdedigers via Dasa naar Ouaissa, waarbij AZ kortstondig een numeriek overwicht had aan de “vrijere” rechterkant. Bij balbezit van Ouaissa vóór de 2:0 stonden 5 (!) spelers van N.E.C. nog links functieloos, niet betrokken naast elkaar – dus ook aansluitende bewegingen om kleine-aantallenpatronen te ondersteunen of doelgerichte loopacties en voorzetvoorbereidingen ontbraken. Sandler, die de verplaatsing bij de 2:0 inleidde, liep na zijn pass naar de zijkant door naar voren (kennelijk een principe van Nijmegen). Echter op zo’n manier dat hij Ouaissa in het 1-tegen-1 blokkeerde, daarna niet als ondersteunende speler fungeerde en eigenlijk enigszins doelloos voor hem stond. Door de loopactie van Sandler liet Nejasmic zich duidelijk in de laatste linie zakken en ook Dasa zag ervan af om Ouaissa korter te ondersteunen, waardoor hij in een 1-tegen-2 terechtkwam. Uiteindelijk leidde dit door de ondertal-situatie tot balverlies van Nijmegen – mede door het ontbreken van een “bodyguard” van Dasa. Sandler stond voor de bal, het centrum was onbezet, AZ kon eenvoudig naar voren spelen en aanvallen – doordat het in de restverdediging ontbrak aan situatie-inzicht (Nejasmic) en consequente afdekking. Uiteindelijk verslechterde Sandlers loopactie de situatie eerder.

    Ook aan de derde tegentreffer ging een verplaatsing van links naar rechts vooraf, dit keer liep Dasa als passer niet door – wat in tegenstelling tot Sandler bij de tweede tegentreffer passend zou zijn geweest – maar bood zich opnieuw kort aan – echter verloor Ouaissa zich opnieuw in een ondertal-dribbel (individuele besluitvorming, maar ook weinig ondersteuning). Dit keer was de situatie echter ideaal voor counter-press, waartoe de omliggende Nijmegen-spelers ook besloten, alleen dekte Dasa niet door, waardoor AZ min of meer gecontroleerd kon uitspelen. Met enig geluk wist AZ, opnieuw achter de laatste verdediger (Sandler) van N.E.C., maar nog op eigen helft, door te spelen en de 3:0 te maken. In het vervolg probeerde Nijmegen alles, maar behalve korte hoop na de 3:1 kwam er niets meer.

    According to recent reports, N.E.C. draaide zo ver aan de knop van positiewisselingen dat het bijna oververhit raakte. Constante over-overloads, nieuwe posities, verticaal doordribbelende centrale verdedigers uit een driemansopbouw zijn een grote, in deze wedstrijd tegen een slim verdedigend AZ, te grote last om tegelijkertijd spelritme, veldcontrole en restorganisatie in het oog te houden. Te veel spelers, bijvoorbeeld Sano als linker, afzakkende zes uit de overload, die bij balbezit van Ouaissa twee keer niet consequent genoeg naast de laatste verdediger van N.E.C. doorschoof voor een 2-tegen-1-afdekking, moeten in situaties verdedigen of aanvallen (Sandler voor de 2:0) die te vreemd/te ongeschikt of te veeleisend zijn qua situatiedynamiek voor hun profiel.

    According to recent reports, desondanks is Nijmegen een team dat zich door hun vrij-radicale speelstijl heeft toegelegd op aantrekkelijk, onderhoudend voetbal. Uitstekende aanzetten zouden offensief door eenvoud, consistentie (positiegetrouwheid) en teamorganisatie (ritme van de aanvalsrichting, balans van overloads) kunnen worden verbeterd. Defensief zou een collectiviteit van de laatste linie zijn intrede moeten doen. Mocht dit in de toekomst lukken, zal N.E.C. niet alleen als een van de spannendste teams van Nederland voor ophef zorgen, maar ook in Europa. Als derde in de Eredivisie zijn ze in ieder geval op de goede weg.

    HH groeide op aan de Nederlandse grens, maar oriënteerde zich tactisch liever richting Zuid-Europa. Naast freelancewerkzaamheden voor Duitse profclubs is hij sinds twee jaar ook actief als jeugdtrainer bij de O17 van N.E.C. Nijmegen.

    Industry News: 49ers lose shot at breaking NFL record for most miles traveled due to Week 11 travel detour en route to Mexico

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (381 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With a trip to Australia in Week 1 and a trip to Mexico City in Week 11, the expectation before the season started was that the 49ers were going to break the NFL record for most miles traveled this season, but that's actually not going to happen due to a travel detour that the team is taking this week.
    • It has been revealed that after beating the Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers didn't fly home to California.
    • The 49ers' decision to head to Colorado will reduce the total number of miles the team travels this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With a trip to Australia in Week 1 and a trip to Mexico City in Week 11, the expectation before the season started was that the 49ers were going to break the NFL record for most miles traveled this season, but that's actually not going to happen due to a travel detour that the team is taking this week.

    It has been revealed that after beating the Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers didn't fly home to California. Instead, they took a flight to Colorado, where they spent the week getting acclimated to the high altitude in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet.

    The 49ers' decision to head to Colorado will reduce the total number of miles the team travels this year.

    It has been revealed that if the 49ers had flown home after their game against the Cowboys, they would have traveled a total of 2,876 miles round trip. After that, their round-trip flight to Mexico City would have covered 3,702 miles for a two-week total of 6,578 miles.

    However, since the 49ers didn't fly home after playing the Cowboys, that will lead to a drastic change in their mileage total. Here's what their Week 10 to Week 11 travel will look like (the 49ers fly out of San Jose):.

    Total for all four: 5,257 miles.

    According to recent reports, the decision to practice in Colorado this week will cut their total travel by 1,321 miles this year, trimming their season total from 38,105 miles to 36,784. At that number, they won't set the NFL's mileage record.

    The Los Angeles Chargers set the record for most travel miles last season when they flew 37,086 miles, and that record will stand for at least another year thanks to the 49ers' decision to take a pit stop in Colorado before heading to Mexico City in Week 11.

    Recent findings suggest that that being said, the 49ers will be setting one NFL record when they take the field on Sunday: They'll become the first team in NFL history to play two international games in two different countries in non-consecutive weeks. The Vikings played in Ireland and England last season, but that came in back-to-back weeks. The 49ers' two international trips are coming 10 weeks apart.
