    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

    Como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

    It has been revealed that cesc Fàbregas’s side revealed two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

    This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

    In a recent development, in build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

    Sources indicate that close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

    Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

    In a recent development, one detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

    ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

    Sources indicate that for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

    The decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

    What made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

    Industry observers note that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

    Recent findings suggest that when the build-up ran down the right, it showed in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

    Recent findings suggest that in the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

    In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

    Sources indicate that especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the latest ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

    It has been revealed that como bridged the middle third exceptionally promptly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

    In this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

    The connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

    Industry observers note that in the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

    The intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

    According to recent reports, paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

    As the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

    Recent findings suggest that what carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

    Sources indicate that united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

    There were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

    Recent findings suggest that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

    On top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

    The second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened new spaces.

    According to recent reports, in the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

    In a recent development, como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

    The steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

    Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

    In the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

    Sources indicate that that isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

    Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

    Sources indicate that once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

    The double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

    The last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

    It has been revealed that when Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

    In the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

    Sources indicate that up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

    Recent findings suggest that the pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

    It has been revealed that at half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

    ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

    The effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

    In the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

    It has been revealed that accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

    Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

    The crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

    It has been revealed that the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

    Tracking the ball for the first goal.

    1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick promptly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

    Sources indicate that what follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

    2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

    The result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

    In a recent development, 3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

    4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and indicates the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

    It has been revealed that como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

    4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

    In a recent development, the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

    Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

    The connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

    According to recent reports, for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

    That leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What highlighted regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

    #50312. A la recherche du Diamant de l'Ange vert

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1221 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Poteaux-carres ↗ Open Full Page

    A la recherche du Diamant de l'Ange vert

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal.
    • Recent findings suggest that "C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer.
    • J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. L'Ange Vert revient dans ce bouquin - anecdotes à l'appui - sur la Rocheteaumania qui a envahi la France après le mythique quart de finale retour de Coupe d'Europe des Clubs Champions qui s'est déroulé le 17 mars 1976 dans le Chaudron. Extraits.

    Recent findings suggest that "C'est seulement le lendemain de notre victoire contre Kiev, puis dans les jours qui ont suivi, que j'ai commencé à prendre la mesure de ce qui venait de se passer. Peu à peu, j'ai perçu l'ampleur de cette vague verte qui n'allait cesser de grandir, et de ce que ce match allait changer dans ma vie. À l'entraînement, une foule que je n'avais encore jamais vue pour un simple décrassage nous attendait : à l'entrée, à la sortie, tout autour du terrain. Que du vert. Cette fois, j'ai pu saluer mes parents à la sortie du stade, juste avant qu'ils ne reprennent la route. J’étais heureux, bien sûr, mais je l'avoue un peu perdu, déconcerté, face à cet engouement auquel je n'étais absolument pas préparé.

    J'ai vraiment pris conscience que quelque chose avait changé lors de nos déplacements en championnat après Kiev. C'était comme si toute la France était derrière nous. Et puis, il y avait les médias, plus seulement sportifs : Paris Match, Télé 7 Jours, Rock & Folk, Rolling Stones, Salut les copains, Pif Gadget… Je ne lisais pas les journaux, je ne regardais pas la télévision. J'étais un peu dans mon monde, mais désormais je devais « apprendre » à me raconter. J'acceptais les demandes, plus par politesse que par réelle envie. Je me retrouvais souvent pris de court, parfois même paniqué. Je n'avais pas d'agent. Les journalistes passaient par le club pour leurs demandes d'interview, et je me sentais obligé d'accepter. À 20 ans, je ne contrôlais rien. Un jour, je me suis rendu compte que j'avais donné une interview pour un magazine érotique… quand ils m'ont envoyé le numéro. C'est aussi après Kiev que l'on a commencé à m'appeler l’« Ange vert », un surnom que j'ai mis du temps à apprécier.

    In a recent development, ce qui m'a le plus désarçonné, ce sont ces sacs de courriers qui ont commencé à arriver. Que faire de tout ça ? Je lisais quelques lettres, mais il y en avait des milliers. Il y avait de tout : des demandes en mariage, des déclarations d'amour, des confidences, des photos, des messages, comme si nous nous connaissions depuis toujours. Après les vacances d'été et celles de Noël, quand je revenais de Charente-Maritime, le secrétaire de l'AS Saint-Étienne m'invitait à passer récupérer au stade des sacs postaux. « Il y en a plusieurs kilos ». Je devinais à son ton que cela représentait une charge de travail. Ils étaient remplis de lettres et parfois de cassettes audio de filles envoyant des compliments ou des messages, par exemple : « Dominique, j'aimerais bien que l'on se voit ». Certaines glissaient même un chewing-gum à l'intérieur. Beaucoup de lettres venaient de filles. Certaines m'avouaient qu'elles m'aimaient.

    Recent findings suggest that il y avait aussi des plaisanteries comme cette lettre émanant de lycéennes d'un établissement religieux en région parisienne qui suggérait mon mariage avec une fille « de bonne famille » de leur entourage. D'autres donnaient des recettes miracles pour faire cesser les rhumes ou bien améliorer le tonus. Des collégiens racontaient aussi le plaisir qu'ils avaient à chanter pendant leurs cours la chanson « Allez les Verts » pour embêter leurs professeurs. Beaucoup de lettres venaient d'Afrique, où Saint-Étienne était très aimé. Certaines étaient longues, parfois plusieurs pages et vraiment très belles. Mais aussi des pays de l'Est -Pologne, Allemagne de l'Est, Tchécoslovaquie - d'où de nombreux collectionneurs m'envoyaient des photos parues dans les magazines afin que je les signe. J'en reçois encore aujourd'hui au siège du club qui me les fait suivre à chaque fois.

    Mes amis Hugues et Louis - qui habitait à Saint-Héand et préparait son concours du barreau - et moi, nous nous asseyions par terre dans la salle à manger pour trier le courrier. Impossible de répondre à tout le monde. Nous envoyions une photo dédicacée à ceux qui avaient joint une enveloppe timbrée à leur nom. Certains glissaient même un billet de 20 ou 50 francs pour recevoir une photo signée. Nous remettions ensuite les enveloppes à la postière de Saint-Héand qui nous félicitait : « Joli travail ! », avant de les oblitérer. À travers toutes ces petites histoires, j'étais à la fois touché mais aussi terriblement gêné. Tout cela me paraissait énorme, démesuré. Dans la rue, j'appréciais les marques de sympathie même si elles me mettaient mal à l'aise. Je ne savais pas toujours quoi dire, alors je répondais par un sourire.

    Un matin de juillet 1976, j'étais en vacances chez mes parents. Je dormais encore tandis que ma mère et Louis prenaient le café dans le jardin. Un jeune homme s'est présenté derrière le grillage et a demandé à me voir. Ma mère lui a demandé s'il me connaissait. Devant sa réponse affirmative et son insistance, elle a fini par le laisser entrer. Ils sont venus me réveiller. « Il y a un ami qui veut te voir ». Je me suis levé, surpris. « Je ne vous connais pas » -  « Si, je vous ai vu à un match »… « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? » « Un autographe ». Je me suis exécuté et il est reparti ravi. Je suis resté partagé entre la satisfaction de faire plaisir et le malaise de voir ma vie privée ainsi envahie.

    Recent findings suggest that une autre fois, peu après avoir fait construire mon chalet à La Gimont, je suis rentré de l'entraînement et j'ai constaté que mon chat, Diamant, avait disparu. Une femme était venue chez moi, l'avait emmenée et avait fait savoir à mon entourage que si je voulais le récupérer, je devais me rendre personnellement chez elle à Veauche, à une dizaine de kilomètres. Mon ami Louis a tenté de la raisonner, en vain. Que faire ? Il n'était pas question pour moi de céder à ce chantage. Je ne voulais pas y aller, mais je tenais à récupérer mon chat. Yves, le frère de Louis, a alors appelé la gendarmerie de Saint-Galmier. Les gendarmes se sont rendus à Veauche et ont réussi à convaincre la dame de rendre Diamant. Ils n'ont toutefois pas pu le ramener eux-mêmes. Sur leur conseil, Louis a sauté dans sa voiture pour aller le chercher. Quand il est arrivé, le chat était couché sur un coussin, sur une chaise. La femme lui a lancé : « Voyez, il avait déjà pris ses marques. » Grâce à Louis et à l'intervention des gendarmes, j'ai pu récupérer Diamant et une fois de plus mesurer la chance que j'avais d'avoir des amis en or. 1976 a été une année folle. Depuis Kiev, tout avait changé autour de moi, mais je n'ai jamais vraiment cherché à me protéger ni à mettre de la distance entre moi et les autres. Je voulais simplement vivre une vie normale, comme les autres jeunes de mon époque.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
    • Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.
    • Industry observers note that just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side highlighted some life late on.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    Industry observers note that just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side highlighted some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    It has been revealed that aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

    Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7.

    Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

    It has been revealed that the final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

    According to recent reports, victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i.

    The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

    It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

    There will be four added minutes.

    In a recent development, when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

    Recent findings suggest that gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

    According to recent reports, for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

    Sources indicate that maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

    Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

    Sources indicate that boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

    Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

    Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

    Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

    Industry observers note that A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

    Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

    Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

    That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

    It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

    Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

    Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

    It has been revealed that just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

    Industry observers note that good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

    Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

    Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

    Sources indicate that tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

    According to recent reports, bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

    We are back under way in Hong Kong.

    The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

    There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

    According to recent reports, aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

    Industry observers note that the German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

    According to recent reports, that is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

    Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

    Recent findings suggest that the first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

    That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

    It has been revealed that bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

    It has been revealed that bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

    Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is at the moment out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

    Industry observers note that the ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

    Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

    Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

    The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

    According to recent reports, the first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

    Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

    It has been revealed that both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

    Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

    Sources indicate that currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. To achieve that; to win the Bundesliga, the cup and the Champions League, we need the whole squad to be fit and healthy. We need to make good use of them and improve the squad. We have already done that, but hopefully it will help us achieve our goals.”.

    Your Aston Villa team to face Bayern Munich in Hong Kong 👊 pic.twitter.com/VxyopTRMFp.

    Here's how we line up to face Aston Villa 🔴𝗪𝗔𝗧𝗖𝗛 𝗟𝗜𝗩𝗘! From 13:55 👉 https://t.co/gFwG0Y99m8#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/JmkEytIjIF.

    July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa’s preparations for the latest season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

    Industry observers note that after losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some latest faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

    In a recent development, unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

    Industry observers note that bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

    In a recent development, after today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Comme l'a souligné hier La Dernière Heure Les Sports +, les candidats ne manquent pas mais le Diablotin Lucas Stassin part de loin. Extraits.

    "Charles De Ketelaere a pris le relais, dans un autre style mais sans être remis en question. Il est le titulaire incontesté en pointe, même s'il joue à une autre position à l'Atalanta. Il sera d'ailleurs intéressant de voir s'il osera prendre le n°9 au prochain rassemblement. Qui pour doubler CDK dorénavant ? Le casting est large et étonnamment ouvert.

    Sources indicate that loïs Openda peut y penser, lui qui retrouvait peu à peu ses sensations à Lyon avant de se blesser et de manquer ce rassemblement. Mais parviendra-t-il enfin à éclore en équipe nationale alors qu'il fêtera bientôt son 27e anniversaire ? Il n'a inscrit que trois buts chez les Diables jusqu'à présent.

    Hugo Cuypers, le Belge le plus prolifique ces derniers mois, peut espérer monter en grade après avoir fêté sa première sélection. Mais lui aura 30 ans au prochain rassemblement. Il ne sera pas une solution à long terme et devra aussi prouver qu'il peut avoir le niveau en évoluant dans le championnat mexicain.

    Recent findings suggest that L'avant-centre le plus prometteur en Belgique, c'est probablement Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21 ans), mais avec un tout autre profil que Lukaku et De Ketelaere. Acheté 60 M€ par Newcastle cet été, il possède une vitesse et une puissance de jambes assez phénoménales. Le tout avec un vrai sens du but.

    Industry observers note that le sélectionneur a aussi une autre option, très différente : le faux 9. Deux joueurs sont capables de prendre ce rôle, que CDK peut parfois avoir selon le moment du match. On pense à Leandro Trossard, qui avait par moments dépanné Arsenal devant, et à Mika Godts, barré sur les flancs par Jeremy Doku et Diego Moreira. Lui aussi a déjà évolué en faux 9, à l'Ajax.

    In a recent development, L'idée sera aussi de regarder dans le réservoir belge. En Espoirs, trois attaquants prouvent qu'ils ont des qualités : Lucas Stassin, Romeo Vermant et Norman Bassette. À tel point que le coach Gill Swerts a cherché un système pour en utiliser au moins deux des trois en même temps. Leur évolution en club fera beaucoup de leur avenir à court terme chez les Diables.".

    • In a recent development, S'il n'a pas encore joué de match officiel en équipe première sous le maillot vert depuis son arrivée dans le Forez le 2 février dernier, Marten-Chris Paalberg, actuellement sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en 2030, a démarré cet automne 3 matches avec la réserve : 1 en Challenge Espoirs (0-2 face au Mans) et 2 en National 2 (1-1 à Montpellier).
    • "Je suis maintenant en pleine forme !
    • Industry observers note that pour être honnête, je ne sais pas exactement quel était mon problème au genou.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, S'il n'a pas encore joué de match officiel en équipe première sous le maillot vert depuis son arrivée dans le Forez le 2 février dernier, Marten-Chris Paalberg, actuellement sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en 2030, a démarré cet automne 3 matches avec la réserve : 1 en Challenge Espoirs (0-2 face au Mans) et 2 en National 2 (1-1 à Montpellier). Venant d'enchaîner 2 succès en équipe d'Estonie (le premier en sortie de banc au Luxembourg et le second en tant que titulaire contre la Bulgarie), le prometteur attaquant de 18 ans s'est longuement confié à Soccernet. Un long et intéressant entretien que nous avons traduit pour vous !

    "Je suis maintenant en pleine forme ! Nouveau club, nouvel environnement. Je pense avoir progressé et maintenant, je vais pouvoir le montrer. Ma santé actuellement ? Disons que tout va bien. Comme j'ai eu des problèmes au genou pendant très longtemps, il arrive que, lorsque les entraînements ou les matchs sont particulièrement intenses, je ressente quelques sensations différentes le lendemain. Mais pour le moment, tout va bien. J'enchaîne les matchs, j'accumule du temps de jeu et je n'ai aucune raison de me plaindre.

    Industry observers note that pour être honnête, je ne sais pas exactement quel était mon problème au genou. Tout ce que je peux dire, c'est qu'il y avait un problème au niveau de la rotule et du tendon. À la fin, c'est devenu chronique, ce qui explique pourquoi cela a pris autant de temps. Mais je ne connais pas exactement le diagnostic de mémoire. Je n'ai aucune restriction, mais au sein de l'équipe, on souhaite que je prenne un jour de repos supplémentaire en milieu de semaine après les journées les plus intenses. Ce n'est pas vraiment une restriction, puisque c'est aussi une journée de récupération pour le reste de l'équipe. De mon côté, je fais simplement quelques exercices avec les kinés à l'intérieur.

    Industry observers note that mon adaptation et ma vie en France ? J'ai maintenant pris mes marques. Je suis également devenu plus proche de mes coéquipiers et nous sortons régulièrement ensemble. L'année dernière, c'était un peu plus compliqué, mais maintenant tout est facile et tout va bien. Je m'entraîne tous les jours avec les professionnels. Pour le moment, je joue simplement avec la réserve. Mais mon environnement de travail quotidien reste bien celui de l'équipe première.

    Industry observers note that je ne peux pas dire quand je ferai mes débuts en équipe première, c'est à l'entraîneur de décider. Pour le moment, la situation est compliquée : l'équipe première est en haut du classement et les attaquants marquent des buts. De mon côté, je fais simplement mon travail. L'occasion finira par arriver et ce sera alors mon heure de me montrer.

    Comment je décrirais le niveau de la cinquième division française, notamment par rapport à la Première Ligue estonienne ? Je dirais clairement que le niveau est supérieur. Ce n'est pas non plus un immense fossé, mais le jeu est très physique. En face, on retrouve de grands gaillards, et pas des équipes réserves comme la nôtre. Bon, il y a encore un autre club réserve dans le championnat, mais toutes les autres équipes sont composées de joueurs professionnels. Le jeu est très physique et rapide.

    Les séances de l'équipe première sont très intenses et difficiles pour tout le monde. Après l'entraînement, tout le monde termine les mains sur les genoux ! Les premières semaines après mon retour ont été difficiles, mais depuis, les choses vont de mieux en mieux. Je sens que je m'en sors finalement plutôt bien. Les entraîneurs me font également de bons retours et tout me convient.

    According to recent reports, je ne saurais pas dire exactement à quel niveau je me situe par rapport aux autres joueurs de l'effectif pro, mais les entraîneurs insistent certainement auprès de nos jeunes joueurs sur la nécessité d'en faire davantage pour progresser et être prêts à être lancés dans le grand bain. Dans l'ensemble, ça se passe bien. Les entraîneurs veulent que je prenne davantage d'initiatives, que je demande plus souvent le ballon et que je sois encore plus actif. C'est ainsi que je pourrai continuer à progresser.

    J'ai également joué au poste de numéro 10. Si je souhaite qu'on fasse de moi un joueur davantage impliqué dans la construction du jeu ? Oui. Chez nous, aussi bien l'équipe première que la réserve évoluent avec deux attaquants. Dans les deux équipes, l'un des deux décroche légèrement. Avec la réserve, j'ai également un autre attaquant à mes côtés, qui joue plutôt comme un véritable avant-centre.

    De mon côté, je suis davantage un joueur technique et c'est pour cette raison qu'on souhaite me voir évoluer plus souvent au poste de numéro 10. Cela me convient également, car c'est bien d'avoir plusieurs possibilités. En ce moment, je joue surtout à ce poste, voire même en faux numéro 9. J'ai également expliqué aux entraîneurs que, comme j'ai pratiquement toujours joué en tant qu'avant-centre, je préfère clairement évoluer à ce poste pour le moment. C'est celui auquel je suis le plus habitué.

    It has been revealed that jouer numéro 10 avec la réserve reste encore un peu difficile. Il faut s'habituer à évoluer dans un système à deux attaquants. J'aime aussi davantage avoir le ballon et participer au jeu. Aujourd'hui, je dirais que c'est du 50-50 concernant mes préférences, mais pour le moment, j'aimerais quand même jouer davantage tout en haut de l'attaque.

    In a recent development, si je me suis habitué à la vie en France, à la langue française et à tout le reste ? Le français… Je n'ai pas vraiment envie de parler avec les gens, c'est difficile ! (Rires.) Je comprends la langue et nous suivons également des cours de français chaque semaine avec les autres joueurs étrangers. Mais lorsque je me promène en ville, je ne me sens pas encore complètement chez moi. L'environnement est tout de même assez différent, avec davantage de vie urbaine.

    Si les rues de Saint-Etienne sont calmes ? Pas du tout ! Il y a des troubles dans toute la France et nous en avons également chez nous. Il y a eu des jours où dans toute la ville, les magasins étaient fermés et barricadés. Il y avait pas mal d'agitation. Cela ne perturbe pas du tout mes déplacements pour aller à l'entraînement. J'habite assez près et le centre d'entraînement se trouve également dans la partie haute de la ville, où il n'y a pas de gros problèmes.

    In a recent development, J'ai maintenant trouvé un appartement. Le club dispose d'un responsable qui s'occupe des joueurs et de leurs questions liées à la vie quotidienne. Grâce à lui, nous avons trouvé un appartement agréable à proximité. Personnellement, j'aurais préféré habiter un peu plus loin, mais comme je n'ai pas de voiture, cela aurait été un peu compliqué.

    Si je sais me débrouiller tout seul, préparer des pâtes et faire ta lessive ? Bien sûr que je sais faire ! Ma mère s'inquiète beaucoup, mais moi, je m'en sors très bien ! (Rires.) Il n'y a pas vraiment de raison de s'inquiéter. Pour les repas, c'est assez simple : le club dispose d'un service de restauration qui prépare le dîner pour tous les joueurs qui le souhaitent. On peut ensuite récupérer son repas et l'emporter chez soi.

    It has been revealed that mon temps libre, je joue un peu à la PlayStation, mais je sors également avec des amis, notamment les plus jeunes joueurs de l'équipe. Ils parlent français et pas vraiment anglais, donc ce n'est pas toujours évident. Mais ils sont vraiment sympas : ils essaient de baragouiner quelques mots en anglais et, de mon côté, je leur réponds en français. C'est un peu un mélange des deux langues, mais ça fonctionne très bien !

    Recent findings suggest that pour être honnête, cette année a été très difficile pour moi mentalement. Quand je suis arrivé là-bas en février, je voulais évidemment commencer à jouer immédiatement. Mais ensuite, ce problème physique est apparu et la situation s'est prolongée, encore et encore. Heureusement, le club dispose d'un psychologue avec qui il est très facile de discuter. Je lui confie régulièrement tout ce que j'ai sur le cœur et il m'a énormément aidé. Ma famille, mes amis et mon agent m'ont également beaucoup soutenu.

    Sources indicate that maintenant, ça va mieux. Je joue et je n'ai plus de problème. Il faut simplement continuer à avancer. Je n'ai pas vraiment souffert du mal du pays pendant cette période car j'ai toujours voulu vivre à l'étranger et mener une carrière de footballeur à l'étranger. Pour moi, cela a été assez facile, mais vous pouvez imaginer ce que ma famille a pu ressentir… Ma mère pleurait régulièrement au téléphone, alors que de mon côté, je le vivais plutôt bien. Je ne me faisais pas de souci à ce sujet. Je voulais simplement guérir et recommencer à jouer.

    L'année dernière, lorsque j'étais en sélection en novembre, j'ai commencé à ressentir quelque chose vers la fin du rassemblement, avant le match contre Chypre. Mais ensuite, la douleur a disparu. Tout semblait simple, je n'avais aucun problème et je m'entraînais normalement. Mais il est possible que le rythme ait été particulièrement intense avec l'équipe première. Là-bas non plus, je n'avais pas vraiment de repos : j'ai immédiatement repris le travail et le même problème est revenu. La différence de charge de travail a donc pu jouer un rôle.

    Si cela pourrait être lié à la croissance ? Certainement. Il faut aussi prendre en compte le fait que l'année dernière, lorsque je jouais au Vaprus, j'étais également présent à chaque rassemblement international avec les différentes sélections. Je ne prenais donc pas de repos, contrairement aux autres joueurs qui avaient tout de même quelques jours de congé. À chaque retour de sélection, je reprenais immédiatement l'entraînement et les matchs s'enchaînaient.

    Ma taille ? 1,85 m. Cela fait déjà quelque temps. Dans quelle mesure le changement d'entraîneur l'été dernier à Saint-Etienne cela a modifié ou influencé ma situation ? Cela n'a rien changé. Lorsqu'il est arrivé, nous avons immédiatement discuté et il m'a dit qu'il m'appréciait et qu'il me voyait dans ses prepares. Il fallait simplement que je retrouve la pleine forme et que je puisse désormais lui montrer progressivement ce dont je suis capable.".

    Industry observers note that chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Sources indicate that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

    Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

    Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

    Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

    AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    He is among the newly introduced breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

    It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

    According to recent reports, chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

    AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

    Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

    Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

    Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

    Time for the second half water break.

    Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and rapidly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

    Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

    AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

    AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

    Sources indicate that palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

    Recent findings suggest that ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

    Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

    According to recent reports, chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

    In a recent development, AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their newly introduced record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

    Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

    Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2.

    The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

    90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

    Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

    Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

    The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

    Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

    It has been revealed that then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

    Sources indicate that the space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

    Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

    It has been revealed that we will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

    Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

    That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

    According to recent reports, chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

    Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

    A significant, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

    Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

    It has been revealed that neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

    Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

    Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

    Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

    Sources indicate that we are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

    It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

    The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

    The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    According to recent reports, yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have fresh managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso mentioned in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so notable to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    Industry observers note that AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their substantial-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    According to recent reports, L'ancien Vert, Maedine Makhloufi, transféré à l'US Dunkerque le 13 janvier dernier foulera peut-être la pelouse de Geoffroy-Guichard le samedi 28 novembre prochain avec le FC Villefranche Beaujolais, pour le 8ème tour de la Coupe de France. En effet, le club caladois annonce le prêt du latéral gauche par le club nordiste : "Nous sommes heureux d’annoncer l’arrivée de Maedine Makhloufi, prêté par l’USL Dunkerque jusqu’à la fin de la saison !Formé à l’AS Saint Etienne de ses 8 ans jusqu’au monde senior, il signe en Ligue 2, à Dunkerque, l’an dernier."Maedine Makhloufi espère faire partie du onze qui viendra défier les Verts en Coupe de France : "Je suis très heureux d’être prêté au FCVB et de retrouver une région que je connais et que j’apprécie ! Le hasard du tirage va me faire retrouver l’ASSE et le chaudron. J’espère que ce sera un beau match et que le meilleur gagne".

    Il va retrouver à Villefranche un autre ancien Vert, le défenseur central Marvin Tshibuabua.

    Recent findings suggest that maedine Makhloufi était en manque de temps de jeu avec l'US Dunkerque :  sur les 12 rencontres disputées en Ligue 2, il n'a pas été retenu dans le groupe à 8 reprises, est resté sur le banc sans entrer à 3 reprises et n'est entré que pour 9 petites minutes contre Rodez le 30 octobre. La saison dernière, sur 16 matchs disputés par Dunkerque, il avait été titulaire à 3 reprises, était entré en jeu à 5 reprises. Lors de son entrée pour 4 minutes face à Boulogne, il avait inscrit 1 but lors de ce derby qui avait vu Dinkerque l'emporetr par 6 à 2.Avec les Verts, Maedine Makhloufi n'a disputé qu'un seul match en pro, contre la modeste équipe de Quetigny à Dijon en Coupe de France.

    Breaking: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.
